questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: (1) The international tribunal identified the specific military commanders / (2) to whose oversight the war crimes were directly attributed to / (3) during the formal presentation of evidence by the chief prosecutor / (4) at the international court of justice.
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(1) The international tribunal identified the specific military commanders / (2) to whose oversight the war crimes were directly attributed to / (3) during the formal presentation of evidence by the chief prosecutor / (4) at the international court of justice.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. to whose oversight the war crimes were directly attributed to .

Key Points

  • The error in the sentence lies in the phrase, "to whose oversight the war crimes were directly attributed to."
  • In English grammar, it is incorrect to end a clause with a redundant preposition like "to" when it is already used earlier in the phrase.
  • The correct way to phrase it would be "to whose oversight the war crimes were directly attributed," without the second "to."

Correct sentence: The international tribunal identified the specific military commanders to whose oversight the war crimes were directly attributed during the formal presentation of evidence by the chief prosecutor at the international court of justice.

Additional Information

  • Common Redundancy Errors:
    • Redundant prepositions are a frequent grammatical error in English.
    • Example of redundancy: "Where are you going to?" Correct version: "Where are you going?"
  • Key to Avoiding Redundancy:
    • Ensure that prepositions are used only where necessary and avoid repeating them.
    • Always revise sentences to eliminate unnecessary words or phrases.

These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find out which of the four combinations is correct.

S1. Soil erosion is one of the most serious environmental and public health problems facing human society.

P.  Humans obtain more than 99.7% of their food (calories) from the land and less than 0.3% from the oceans and other aquatic ecosystems.

Q. Each year about 10 million ha of cropland are lost due to soil erosion.

R. Thus reducing the cropland available for food production.

S. The loss of cropland is a serious problem because the World Health Organization reports that more than 3.7 billion people are malnourished in the world.

S6. Overall soil is being lost from land areas 10 to 40 times faster than the rate of soil renewal imperiling future human food security and environmental quality.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'PQRS'.

Key Points

  •  While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some grammatical or contextual connections between them-
    • P follows sentence 1 as the noun 'Humans' mentioned in 'P' refers back to "human society" in sentence 1.
    • Next is Q as the noun 'cropland' mentioned in 'Q' refers back to the noun 'land' in 'P'.
    • After that is 'R' as it described the result of what has mentioned in 'Q'.
    • Last is S as it describes how serious the problem of the loss of cropland is.
  • Thus, the correct order is PQRS:
     

1. Soil erosion is one of the most serious environmental and public health problems facing human society.
P. Humans obtain more than 99.7% of their food (calories) from the land and less than 0.3% from the oceans and other aquatic ecosystems.
Q. Each year about 10 million ha of cropland are lost due to soil erosion.
R. Thus reducing the cropland available for food production.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- '​Unconscionable'

Key Points

  • Let us see the meanings of the given option:
    • Egregious:
      • The word "Egregious" is derived from Latin ēgregius, from e- (“out of”), + grex (“flock”), + English adjective suffix -ous, from Latin suffix -osus (“full of”). It means outstandingly bad; shocking.
      • Word "Egregious" लैटिन एग्रेगियस से लिया गया है, जो ई- ("आउट ऑफ"), + ग्रीक्स ("झुंड"), + अंग्रेजी विशेषण प्रत्यय -ous, लैटिन प्रत्यय -ओसस ("पूर्ण") से लिया गया है। इसका अर्थ है असाधारण रूप से खराब; चौंका देने वाला।
        • Example: It was an egregious error for a statesman to show such ignorance.​
    • Unconscionable:
      • The word "Unconscionable" is derived from Mid 16th century from un-'not' + obsolete conscionable, from conscience(interpreted as a plural) + -able.
      • Word "Unconscionable"  16 वीं शताब्दी के मध्य से गैर-'नहीं' + अप्रचलित विवेकशील, विवेक से (बहुवचन के रूप में व्याख्या किया गया) + -योग्य से लिया गया है।
        • Example: This unconscionable policy will cause great suffering.
    • Glib:
      • The word "Glib" is derived from German glibberig which means "smooth, slippery." It means fluent but insincere and shallow.
      • Word "Glib" जर्मन ग्लिबेरिग से लिया गया है जिसका अर्थ है "चिकना, फिसलन।" इसका अर्थ है धाराप्रवाह लेकिन निष्ठाहीन और उथला।
        • Example: The glib phrases soon roll off the tongue.
  • ​Therefore, morally unacceptable is called 'Unconscionable.'

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The song what you performed right before intermission is my favorite.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

The song what you performed right before intermission is my favorite.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'that you performed​.'Key Points

  • The error lies in 'what you performed' part of the sentence.
  • "What" indicates the object in the question itself, or the entire larger set.
    • Example: What would you like to do?
  • The relative pronoun 'who' is used mainly for people.
    • Example: The musician who wrote this song is Indian.
  • The relative pronoun 'which' is used for animals in general or non-living things.
    • ​Example: Raghav bought the top hybrid car, which will help him save on gas.
  • "That" can introduce an explanatory dependent clause and "What" cannot.
  • "That" indicates specific quality of the object in question or a subset of a larger set.
    • Example: This is the cat that killed the rat.
  • Therefore, the use of 'what you performed' should be replaced by' that you performed' to make it grammatically correct.
  • ​​Correct sentence: The song that you performed right before intermission is my favorite.

Additional Information
 
 
 

  • The present tense is the base form of the verb.
  • We use do and does to make questions with the present simple.
  • We use does for the third person singular (she/he/it) and do for the others.
  • We use do and does with question words like where, what and when.
    • Example: Where do Angela and Rita live?

Hinglish

  • त्रुटि वाक्य के भाग 'what you performed'  में है।
  • "What" प्रश्न में ही वस्तु या पूरे बड़े सेट को इंगित करता है।
    • Example: What would you like to do?
  • Relative pronoun 'which' का प्रयोग सामान्यतया जानवरों या चीजों के लिए किया जाता है।
    • Example: Raghav bought the top hybrid car, which will help him save on gas.
  • "That" एक व्याख्यात्मक आश्रित खंड पेश कर सकता है और "What" नहीं कर सकता।
  • "That" प्रश्न में वस्तु की विशिष्ट गुणवत्ता या बड़े सेट के सबसेट को इंगित करता है।
    • Example: This is the cat that killed the rat.
  • इसलिए वाक्य के 'what you performed'  प्रयोग को 'that you performed' से बदल देना चाहिए ताकि वह व्याकरण की दृष्टि से सही हो।​

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 (Relentlessly unyielding and impossible to stop).

Key Points

  • The word "inexorably" means in a manner that is impossible to stop or prevent; relentlessly, unyieldingly. (अपरिहार्य रूप से)
    • Example: Time moves inexorably forward, regardless of human desires.
  • "Relentlessly unyielding and impossible to stop" conveys the same sense of inevitability and unstoppable force. (दृढ़तापूर्वक और अजेय)
    • Example: The army advanced in a relentlessly unyielding manner, leaving no chance for retreat.
  • Hence, we can infer that the synonym of 'inexorably' is 'relentlessly unyielding and impossible to stop'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: Entirely accidental and random (पूरी तरह आकस्मिक और यादृच्छिक) – This suggests unpredictability, which is the opposite of inexorability.
    • Example: His success was entirely accidental, depending on random chance.
  • Option 3: Deliberately deceptive and manipulated (जानबूझकर धोखेबाज़ और हेरफेर किया हुआ) – This implies intentional trickery, unrelated to the unstoppable nature of inexorability.
    • Example: The report was deliberately deceptive to secure funding.
  • Option 4: Highly flexible and porous (अत्यधिक लचीला और छिद्रपूर्ण) – This suggests adaptability, which is the opposite of being rigid and unstoppable.
    • Example: Modern theories are highly flexible and porous, open to reinterpretation.
